symbols.name: formal variable
symbols.meaning: A formal variable in which the polynomials of this page are written; it is a symbol, not a number.
symbols.quote: Identify $a$ with $a(w) = \sum_{s=0}^{n-1} a_s w^s$, where $w$ is a formal variable (a symbol, not a number).

symbols.name: multiplier
symbols.meaning: A positive integer with a modular inverse modulo $n_\kappa$, one for each axis.
symbols.quote: The layout relies on a [Modular inverse](modular-inverse.md) modulo $n_\kappa$ for each multiplier $\mu_\kappa$, which is a positive integer.

symbols.name: axis variable
symbols.meaning: The variable of axis $\kappa$, whose $n_\kappa$-th power is $1$.
symbols.quote: Let $\nu_\kappa$ be the variable of axis $\kappa$, with $\nu_\kappa^{n_\kappa} = 1$

symbols.name: layout map
symbols.meaning: The map sending $w$ to the product of the axis variables raised to the powers $\mu_\kappa$.
symbols.quote: let $\Phi$ be the map that sends $w$ to $\prod_\kappa \nu_\kappa^{\mu_\kappa}$.

symbols.name: axis index
symbols.meaning: An index $1 \le \kappa \le D$ numbering the axes; on this page it is not the constant of the time bound.
symbols.quote: Here $\kappa$ is an axis index, not the constant $\kappa$ of the time bound, and axis $\kappa$ has length $n_\kappa$, the number of values its coordinate takes.

symbols.name: axis length
symbols.meaning: The number of values the coordinate of axis $\kappa$ takes.
symbols.quote: Here $\kappa$ is an axis index, not the constant $\kappa$ of the time bound, and axis $\kappa$ has length $n_\kappa$, the number of values its coordinate takes.

symbols.name: phase sequence
symbols.meaning: The phase $e^{-\pi i s^2/q}$ at position $s$, used only in the middle-transform identity.
symbols.quote: Let $\phi_s = e^{-\pi i s^2/q}$ and $\psi_\delta = e^{\pi i \delta^2/q}$ for integers $s$ and $\delta$; here $\phi$ and $\psi$ are local names, used only in this section.

symbols.name: phase kernel
symbols.meaning: The sequence $e^{\pi i \delta^2/q}$ at offset $\delta$, used only in the middle-transform identity.
symbols.quote: Let $\phi_s = e^{-\pi i s^2/q}$ and $\psi_\delta = e^{\pi i \delta^2/q}$ for integers $s$ and $\delta$; here $\phi$ and $\psi$ are local names, used only in this section.

relations.quote: A cyclic convolution of length $n$ is split by the [Chinese remainder theorem](chinese-remainder-theorem.md) into a $D$-dimensional cyclic convolution when $n = n_1 \cdots n_D$ with $n_1, \dots, n_D$ pairwise coprime (no common factor above 1).
The layout relies on a [Modular inverse](modular-inverse.md) modulo $n_\kappa$ for each multiplier $\mu_\kappa$, which is a positive integer.
